# Autopilot: end-to-end vibecoding orchestrator — brief to working project in one dialogue

Curated by Skill Harbor — @nick-vels's Autopilot: a self-contained orchestrator that flies a dictated app, site, bot or feature from words to a working project in one dialogue, without making the user approve each stage. The brief becomes a numbered manifest first ("nothing may quietly vanish"), then nine gated phases (preflight, manifest, briefing, spec, plan, subagents, review, final) with four modes — full, semi (default), interview, manual — and dials for depth (strict/deep) and finish (polish). Five rules never lose: requirements are removed only by the user, secrets are never requested/echoed/written (redaction gate at ingest, .env in .gitignore before the first commit), facts about the user are never invented, irreversible actions are questions, and the orchestrator never writes project code itself. Includes an instruments dashboard (state.js + dashboard.html), project memory (the .autopilot/ folder is committed as the run's record), and blind acceptance at the end. MIT-licensed. Honest notes: the user-facing chat and dashboard use exactly one Russian word per stage (Подготовка, Требования, Брифинг…) while the docs are English — bilingual by design, not by accident; and it's a heavy methodology, so expect a long run for a long build. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
